name: Chinmogging

card.summary: Having a stronger, more defined chin than another person, used as a comparison of jaw-area aesthetics.

quick.overview:
Chinmogging is looksmaxxing slang for having a stronger chin than someone else. It applies the community's term "mogging", meaning outdoing another person in a feature, to the chin specifically.

It matters because the chin is part of the lower-face profile that people use to judge facial structure, so chin comparisons feed into how users think about which features to improve.
quick.how: The term is used descriptively when comparing photos or profiles. People who want a stronger chin discuss options such as weight loss, posture, chin implants, genioplasty or filler, covered in their own entries.
quick.risks: As a term it carries no risk. The procedures people discuss to improve chin projection have their own surgical or injectable risks.

lead: Chinmogging is a looksmaxxing term for having a stronger chin than another person. People use it to compare chin projection and definition in photos and profiles, and to decide whether the chin is a feature worth improving in their own face.

It combines "mogging", slang for visually outdoing someone, with the chin as the compared feature. Mogging is traced by linguists to the acronym AMOG, "alpha male of the group", which spread from manosphere communities and shifted toward physical comparison. [2] The chin contributes to the profile and lower third of the face, and a chiselled jaw and chin are part of the ideal described in mainstream explainers of looksmaxxing. [3]

People who want to improve their own chin discuss changes in body fat, posture and cosmetic procedures such as implants, genioplasty or filler; press coverage of the movement has described chin extensions among the procedures young men pursue. [1] No published research studies the term itself.

chain: Compare chin projection with another person
Identify a weaker chin as a feature to improve
angle.text: Chinmogging is a comparison term rather than a method. It frames the chin as a measurable point of advantage and leads users toward the chin-improvement options covered in related entries.

infobox: Having a stronger chin than another person

paras: The term applies the community's mogging concept to a single feature. A person is said to chinmog another when their chin appears more projected or defined in comparison. Related terms follow the same pattern, such as "framemogged", used when someone appears physically stronger than another. [3]

Looksmaxxing vocabulary developed on incel and manosphere message boards in the 2010s and spread to TikTok in the 2020s, where the "-maxxing" suffix and terms like mogging became widely recognised. [1][4] Mogging itself derives from AMOG and came to mean outdoing someone in appearance, confidence or status. [2]

Looksmaxxing writers divide approaches into softmaxxing, such as skincare, grooming, clothing and fitness, and hardmaxxing, such as surgery. [1][3] Chin extensions appear in press coverage of the procedures young men pursue, alongside jaw surgery, and clinicians and commentators have raised surgical risks and warned about practices such as bone smashing. [1][3]
